1MCQ1 mark
Let RRR be the relation on the set {1,2,3}\{1,2,3\}{1,2,3} given by R={(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(1,2),(2,3)}R=\{(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(1,2),(2,3)\}R={(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(1,2),(2,3)}. Then RRR is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Reflexive: (a,a)∈R(a,a)\in R(a,a)∈R for all aaa. Symmetric: (a,b)⇒(b,a)(a,b)\Rightarrow(b,a)(a,b)⇒(b,a). Transitive: (a,b),(b,c)⇒(a,c)(a,b),(b,c)\Rightarrow(a,c)(a,b),(b,c)⇒(a,c).

  1. 1

    Reflexive check: every (a,a)(a,a)(a,a) is in RRR.

    (1,1), (2,2), (3,3)∈R⇒R is reflexive(1,1),\ (2,2),\ (3,3)\in R \Rightarrow R \text{ is reflexive}(1,1), (2,2), (3,3)∈R⇒R is reflexive(1,1), (2,2), (3,3)∈R⇒R is reflexive\displaystyle (1,1),\ (2,2),\ (3,3)\in R \Rightarrow R \text{ is reflexive}(1,1), (2,2), (3,3)∈R⇒R is reflexive
  2. 2

    Symmetric check: (1,2)(1,2)(1,2) is in RRR but its reverse is not.

    (1,2)∈R but (2,1)∉R⇒not symmetric(1,2)\in R \text{ but } (2,1)\notin R \Rightarrow \text{not symmetric}(1,2)∈R but (2,1)∈/R⇒not symmetric(1,2)∈R but (2,1)∉R⇒not symmetric\displaystyle (1,2)\in R \text{ but } (2,1)\notin R \Rightarrow \text{not symmetric}(1,2)∈R but (2,1)∈/R⇒not symmetric
  3. 3

    Transitive check: (1,2)(1,2)(1,2) and (2,3)(2,3)(2,3) are in RRR, but (1,3)(1,3)(1,3) is not.

    (1,2),(2,3)∈R but (1,3)∉R⇒not transitive(1,2),(2,3)\in R \text{ but } (1,3)\notin R \Rightarrow \text{not transitive}(1,2),(2,3)∈R but (1,3)∈/R⇒not transitive(1,2),(2,3)∈R but (1,3)∉R⇒not transitive\displaystyle (1,2),(2,3)\in R \text{ but } (1,3)\notin R \Rightarrow \text{not transitive}(1,2),(2,3)∈R but (1,3)∈/R⇒not transitive
    1
  4. 4

    So RRR is reflexive only. Option (A).

Answer(A) reflexive, but neither symmetric nor transitive

Watch out Calling RRR transitive without checking the chain (1,2),(2,3)⇒(1,3)(1,2),(2,3)\Rightarrow(1,3)(1,2),(2,3)⇒(1,3).

The number of equivalence relations on the set {1,2,3}\{1,2,3\}{1,2,3} containing (1,2)(1,2)(1,2) and (2,1)(2,1)(2,1) is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea An equivalence relation must be reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

  1. 1

    Smallest one: add all (a,a)(a,a)(a,a) to the given pairs.

    R1={(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(1,2),(2,1)}R_1=\{(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(1,2),(2,1)\}R1​={(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(1,2),(2,1)}

    R1R_1R1​ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

  2. 2

    Add one more pair, say (2,3)(2,3)(2,3). Symmetry and transitivity force more pairs.

    (3,2)∈R;(1,2),(2,3)∈R⇒(1,3)∈R⇒(3,1)∈R(3,2)\in R;\quad (1,2),(2,3)\in R \Rightarrow (1,3)\in R \Rightarrow (3,1)\in R(3,2)∈R;(1,2),(2,3)∈R⇒(1,3)∈R⇒(3,1)∈R(3,2)∈R;(1,2),(2,3)∈R⇒(1,3)∈R⇒(3,1)∈R\displaystyle (3,2)\in R;\quad (1,2),(2,3)\in R \Rightarrow (1,3)\in R \Rightarrow (3,1)\in R(3,2)∈R;(1,2),(2,3)∈R⇒(1,3)∈R⇒(3,1)∈R

    Adding (1,3)(1,3)(1,3) or (3,1)(3,1)(3,1) instead leads to the same result.

  3. 3

    Then every pair is present, so we get A×AA\times AA×A.

    R2=A×AR_2=A\times AR2​=A×A
  4. 4

    Only R1R_1R1​ and R2R_2R2​ are possible.

    Number of equivalence relations=2\text{Number of equivalence relations}=2Number of equivalence relations=2Number of equivalence relations=2\displaystyle \text{Number of equivalence relations}=2Number of equivalence relations=2
    1
Answer(B) 2\displaystyle 22

Watch out Forgetting that A×AA\times AA×A itself is also an equivalence relation.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Bijection = one-one and onto.

  1. 1

    One-one: let x1,x2∈Rx_1,x_2\in\mathbb{R}x1​,x2​∈R with f(x1)=f(x2)f(x_1)=f(x_2)f(x1​)=f(x2​).

    3−4x1=3−4x23-4x_1=3-4x_23−4x1​=3−4x2​
  2. 2

    Subtract 3 and divide by −4-4−4.

    x1=x2⇒f is one-onex_1=x_2 \Rightarrow f \text{ is one-one}x1​=x2​⇒f is one-onex1=x2⇒f is one-one\displaystyle x_1=x_2 \Rightarrow f \text{ is one-one}x1​=x2​⇒f is one-one
    1
  3. 3

    Onto: let y∈Ry\in\mathbb{R}y∈R. Put f(x)=yf(x)=yf(x)=y and solve for xxx.

    3−4x=y⇒x=3−y4∈R3-4x=y \Rightarrow x=\dfrac{3-y}{4}\in\mathbb{R}3−4x=y⇒x=43−y​∈R3−4x=y⇒x=3−y4∈R\displaystyle 3-4x=y \Rightarrow x=\dfrac{3-y}{4}\in\mathbb{R}3−4x=y⇒x=43−y​∈R
  4. 4

    Check that this xxx maps to yyy.

    f(3−y4)=3−4⋅3−y4=3−(3−y)=y⇒f is ontof\left(\dfrac{3-y}{4}\right)=3-4\cdot\dfrac{3-y}{4}=3-(3-y)=y \Rightarrow f \text{ is onto}f(43−y​)=3−4⋅43−y​=3−(3−y)=y⇒f is ontof(3−y4)=3−4⋅3−y4=3−(3−y)=y⇒f is onto\displaystyle f\left(\dfrac{3-y}{4}\right)=3-4\cdot\dfrac{3-y}{4}=3-(3-y)=y \Rightarrow f \text{ is onto}f(43−y​)=3−4⋅43−y​=3−(3−y)=y⇒f is onto

    Hence fff is one-one and onto, i.e. a bijection.

Question 6Question 8

Question 8 of 20, Level 2

8Short answer2 marks
Show that the relation RRR on the set of integers Z\mathbb{Z}Z defined by R={(a,b):2 divides (a−b)}R=\{(a,b): 2 \text{ divides } (a-b)\}R={(a,b):2 divides (a−b)} is an equivalence relation.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

  1. 1

    Reflexive: for any a∈Za\in\mathbb{Z}a∈Z,

    a−a=0=2×0⇒2∣(a−a)⇒(a,a)∈Ra-a=0=2\times0 \Rightarrow 2\mid(a-a) \Rightarrow (a,a)\in Ra−a=0=2×0⇒2∣(a−a)⇒(a,a)∈Ra−a=0=2×0⇒2∣(a−a)⇒(a,a)∈R\displaystyle a-a=0=2\times0 \Rightarrow 2\mid(a-a) \Rightarrow (a,a)\in Ra−a=0=2×0⇒2∣(a−a)⇒(a,a)∈R
    ½
  2. 2

    Symmetric: let (a,b)∈R(a,b)\in R(a,b)∈R, so a−b=2ka-b=2ka−b=2k, k∈Zk\in\mathbb{Z}k∈Z.

    b−a=−2k=2(−k)⇒2∣(b−a)⇒(b,a)∈Rb-a=-2k=2(-k) \Rightarrow 2\mid(b-a) \Rightarrow (b,a)\in Rb−a=−2k=2(−k)⇒2∣(b−a)⇒(b,a)∈Rb−a=−2k=2(−k)⇒2∣(b−a)⇒(b,a)∈R\displaystyle b-a=-2k=2(-k) \Rightarrow 2\mid(b-a) \Rightarrow (b,a)\in Rb−a=−2k=2(−k)⇒2∣(b−a)⇒(b,a)∈R
    ½
  3. 3

    Transitive: let (a,b),(b,c)∈R(a,b),(b,c)\in R(a,b),(b,c)∈R: a−b=2ka-b=2ka−b=2k, b−c=2mb-c=2mb−c=2m. Add.

    a−c=2k+2m=2(k+m)⇒(a,c)∈Ra-c=2k+2m=2(k+m) \Rightarrow (a,c)\in Ra−c=2k+2m=2(k+m)⇒(a,c)∈Ra−c=2k+2m=2(k+m)⇒(a,c)∈R\displaystyle a-c=2k+2m=2(k+m) \Rightarrow (a,c)\in Ra−c=2k+2m=2(k+m)⇒(a,c)∈R
    ½
  4. 4

    Hence RRR is an equivalence relation.

    ½
AnswerR\displaystyle RR is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, hence an equivalence relation.

Check whether the relation RRR on R\mathbb{R}R defined by R={(a,b):a≤b3}R=\{(a,b): a\le b^3\}R={(a,b):a≤b3} is reflexive, symmetric or transitive.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea To disprove a property, one counter-example is enough.

  1. 1

    Reflexive? Take a=12a=\tfrac12a=21​.

    (12)3=18 and 12≰18⇒(12,12)∉R\left(\tfrac12\right)^3=\tfrac18 \text{ and } \tfrac12\not\le\tfrac18 \Rightarrow \left(\tfrac12,\tfrac12\right)\notin R(21​)3=81​ and 21​≤81​⇒(21​,21​)∈/R(12)3=18 and 12≰18⇒(12,12)∉R\displaystyle \left(\tfrac12\right)^3=\tfrac18 \text{ and } \tfrac12\not\le\tfrac18 \Rightarrow \left(\tfrac12,\tfrac12\right)\notin R(21​)3=81​ and 21​≤81​⇒(21​,21​)∈/R
  2. 2

    So RRR is not reflexive.

    1
  3. 3

    Symmetric? 1≤23=81\le 2^3=81≤23=8, so (1,2)∈R(1,2)\in R(1,2)∈R.

    But 2≰13=1⇒(2,1)∉R\text{But } 2\not\le 1^3=1 \Rightarrow (2,1)\notin RBut 2≤13=1⇒(2,1)∈/RBut 2≰13=1⇒(2,1)∉R\displaystyle \text{But } 2\not\le 1^3=1 \Rightarrow (2,1)\notin RBut 2≤13=1⇒(2,1)∈/R
  4. 4

    So RRR is not symmetric.

    1
  5. 5

    Transitive? Check (3,32)\left(3,\tfrac32\right)(3,23​) and (32,43)\left(\tfrac32,\tfrac43\right)(23​,34​).

    3≤(32)3=278,32≤(43)3=64273\le\left(\tfrac32\right)^3=\tfrac{27}{8},\quad \tfrac32\le\left(\tfrac43\right)^3=\tfrac{64}{27}3≤(23​)3=827​,23​≤(34​)3=2764​3≤(32)3=278,32≤(43)3=6427\displaystyle 3\le\left(\tfrac32\right)^3=\tfrac{27}{8},\quad \tfrac32\le\left(\tfrac43\right)^3=\tfrac{64}{27}3≤(23​)3=827​,23​≤(34​)3=2764​
  6. 6

    Both are in RRR, but (3,43)\left(3,\tfrac43\right)(3,34​) is not.

    3≰(43)3=6427≈2.37⇒(3,43)∉R3\not\le\left(\tfrac43\right)^3=\tfrac{64}{27}\approx2.37 \Rightarrow \left(3,\tfrac43\right)\notin R3≤(34​)3=2764​≈2.37⇒(3,34​)∈/R3≰(43)3=6427≈2.37⇒(3,43)∉R\displaystyle 3\not\le\left(\tfrac43\right)^3=\tfrac{64}{27}\approx2.37 \Rightarrow \left(3,\tfrac43\right)\notin R3≤(34​)3=2764​≈2.37⇒(3,34​)∈/R
  7. 7

    So RRR is not transitive.

    1
AnswerR\displaystyle RR is neither reflexive, nor symmetric, nor transitive.
